items.caseName: JSI Investment Pvt Ltd v. SEBI
items.coram: Justice P.S. Dinesh Kumar (Presiding Officer), Meera Swarup and Dr. Dheeraj Bhatnagar (Technical Members)
items.headline: SAT reserves order on Jane Street's grievance that SEBI withheld material needed for its defence
items.text: The Jane Street group entities, restrained by SEBI's ex parte interim order over alleged BANKNIFTY and NIFTY manipulation with about ₹4,843.57 crore in alleged gains impounded, argued that SEBI had not supplied the underlying material, including counterparty trade details, needed to answer the order, and that this breached natural justice. SEBI replied that only relied-upon documents had to be disclosed at this stage, that around 10 GB of data had already been furnished, and that the request was a delaying tactic. After probing how far disclosure must go at the interim stage, the Tribunal reserved its order.

items.caseName: Consortium of AKB Ventures LLP & Sustainable Projects Private Limited v. Narender Kumar Sharma & Ors.
items.caseNo: I.A. 5202 ND 2025 in C.P. IB 284 (PB) of 2021
items.coram: Mahendra Khandelwal (Judicial Member) and Atul Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Losing resolution applicant cannot force fresh CoC vote in Spaze Towers CIRP
items.text: An unsuccessful prospective resolution applicant in the Spaze Towers insolvency sought to annul the CoC vote that approved a rival plan with 96.42% support, remove the RP and order a re-vote, alleging unequal data-room access, canvassing by company employees and conflicting compliance reports. The Bench found no cogent proof that the RP authorised the canvassing, noted the applicant had data-room access, site visits and the chance to revise its plan, and saw nothing showing the compliance reports swayed the CoC. Holding that participation as a PRA gives no right to have a plan accepted or reconsidered, it dismissed the application.

items.caseName: Neeraj Papers Agencies Ltd v. Rainbow Papers Ltd
items.coram: Chitra Hankare (Judicial Member) and Dr. V. G. Venkata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Rainbow Papers sent into liquidation after its resolution plan collapsed
items.text: Rainbow Papers' 2019 resolution plan was never implemented after the Supreme Court set aside its approval, and the creditor debts were later assigned to the applicant. Financial creditors holding 89.95% of the vote then resolved to liquidate the company. Noting that the successful resolution applicant no longer oversaw the company's assets or litigation, the Bench ordered immediate liquidation and appointed Vikash Jain as liquidator.

items.caseName: Atul Sheth, Liquidator for M/s Captive Foods Private Limited
items.coram: Chitra Hankare (Judicial Member) and Dr. V. G. Venkata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Small pending income tax demands no bar to dissolving assetless Captivate Foods
items.text: The liquidator found no realisable assets: the registered office was rented, the directors could not be traced, and the machinery had already been removed. The Income Tax Department objected over unpaid demands of ₹280 and ₹8,140. The Bench held that continuing the liquidation would serve no purpose, ordered dissolution under Section 54 IBC and discharged the liquidator, while leaving creditors free to pursue the suspended management separately.

items.caseName: Dushyant C. Dave, Liquidator of Siddhi Vinayak Logistic Limited
items.coram: Shammi Khan (Judicial Member) and Sanjeev Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: Siddhi Vinayak Logistic dissolved; pending proceedings left to creditor-nominated banks
items.text: The liquidator had realised about ₹148.61 crore and distributed it, and had assigned the not-readily-realisable assets by auction. SBI chose to enforce its remaining security on its own under SARFAESI. Relying on the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026, the Bench held that pending proceedings do not by themselves bar dissolution once creditors have authorised banks to pursue those proceedings afterwards, and it dissolved the company under Section 54(2).

items.caseName: Sri Kambalipati Haribabu, Representing Sivom Social Welfare Association Members v. Isukapatla Sambamurthy & Others
items.coram: Laxmi Narayana Jannu and K. Srinivasa Rao (Members)
items.headline: Telangana RERA orders penalty action against Sivom Projects and its MD over unregistered layout sales
items.text: The 45-plot Sivom Sahasra II layout in Jeedimetla was well above the Section 3(2)(a) exemption limits, yet plots were sold in 2021–22 without RERA registration. The Authority held Sivom Projects, its MD in his personal capacity and the GPA holder jointly liable as promoters, and directed its Secretary to start Section 59 penalty proceedings. It declined to order completion of works or sale of the mortgaged plots while a High Court status quo order and civil disputes remain pending.
